clue.text: Bad sprain? Take one tablet

indicators.note: a bad sprain is a twisted one, so its letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone with a nasty sprained ankle is advised to swallow a single painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' joins the extra I to the letters of SPRAIN before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkiller usually swallowed as a small pill.

clue.text: Sort of biker regularly wearing glasses

indicators.note: the specs are worn around the picked letters, so they enclose them

parts.note: specs is informal for spectacles, i.e. glasses

indicators.note: taking every other letter of biker, the second and fourth

parts.note: its alternate letters, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist of a certain type always has spectacles on.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or category, so 'sort' is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Usually a leg spinner's angry when powerless to dismiss Stokes at first

indicators.note: an angry mix is a stirred-up one, so the letters are thrown into a new order
dismissing the first letter of Stokes knocks it out of what is left
P is the physics abbreviation for power, so being without power drops that letter

parts.note: the word spinner, with the 's read as part of the surface

indicators.note: the first letter of Stokes

parts.note: first letter S

explanation.surface: A cricket leg-spin bowler is furious when he cannot get England all-rounder Ben Stokes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P from SPINNER for SINNER, then the S (Stokes at first) for INNER; 'angry' rearranges INNER with A LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase in general means as a rule or for the most part, the same idea as usually.

clue.text: Cold killer who finally arrived on Broadway

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nickname for a cold-blooded hitman, as the contract killer Richard Kuklinski was known
second meaning: the title figure of Eugene O'Neill's Broadway play The ... Cometh, the one who 'cometh' or arrives

explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the title of O'Neill's play, whose 'Cometh' is old-fashioned for 'arrives'.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer with no feelings is dubbed by a nickname evoking frozen water, and the same word names the awaited figure in O'Neill's play.

clue.text: Drop line

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a downward slope or fall
second meaning: ancestry or lineage, as in someone's family line

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fall downhill and the lineage a person comes from.

clue.text: English fashion, eg clean style

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A description of British couture as tidy and stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun after English, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement of EG CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is graceful refinement in manner or appearance, a sense of style.

clue.text: European test report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a check is a test or inspection

explanation.surface: An exam result issued somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a person from the Czech Republic, a European country.

clue.text: Eccentric aunt carrying type of bomb in both hands — it's normal

indicators.note: the aunt and the hands carry the bomb letter between them, so it is held inside
the bomb letter ends up in both hands, between the R and the L
an eccentric aunt is an odd one, so her letters are put out of order

parts.note: R and L, abbreviations for right and left hands
an A-bomb is an atomic bomb

explanation.surface: A quirky aunt holding an atom bomb in her hands claims it is nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged aunt gives NATU, followed by the hands R and L; the A of A-bomb is carried in between the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means ordinary or to be expected, in line with what is normal.

clue.text: Local resort repaired Queen's Ride

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, here in a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A seaside resort's fairground attraction, mended and fit for royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of LOCAL RESORT give ROLLERCOAST, and the royal ER completes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollercoaster is a fairground or theme-park attraction on a steep track.

clue.text: Is Lassie on vacation saving a good dog?

indicators.note: the outer letters hold on to, or save, the inner ones

parts.note: 'be' is the base form of the verb 'is'

indicators.note: vacated, i.e. emptied of its middle letters

parts.note: first and last letters L and E

explanation.surface: A question whether the famous film collie, while away, rescues a well-behaved hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lassie' suggests the famous collie, but it only supplies its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound breed used for hunting hares.

clue.text: In books, Peter Pan gets acting work

indicators.note: gets here means acquires as well, so the abbreviation is added on at the end
the rearranged name sits inside the books

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament books of the Bible

indicators.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, so the name is knocked about into a new order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a temporary rank

explanation.surface: J. M. Barrie's boy hero appears in print and lands a stage role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' is read as a verb, to slate, rather than the surname of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera, a musical stage work.

clue.text: Some like sandwiches (honey?)

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer between them, like a sandwich filling

parts.note: the run soME Like

explanation.surface: A question whether some people enjoy honey in their sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel is the Latin word for honey, used in old pharmacy and in crosswords.

clue.text: Former F1 driver takes pole position in shade

indicators.note: the driver's name takes in, or contains, the extra letter

parts.note: Ayrton Senna, the Brazilian Formula One champion
pole position is first place on the starting grid, number one, written I

explanation.surface: A retired racing driver claims the front spot on the grid out of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy reddish-brown colour, so it is a shade of paint.

clue.text: The French hate cooking that's ready on the outside and tough

parts.note: le is the French for 'the'

indicators.note: cooking stirs ingredients up, so these letters are mixed
just the outer letters of ready

parts.note: outer letters R and Y

explanation.surface: French people loathe food that is only done on its surface and chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery describes something hard and chewy like hide, so tough.

clue.text: Rulers, slide rules, algebra, statistics, trigonometry — all initially rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the string is read backwards
the first letter of every one of these words

parts.note: S
R
A
S
T

explanation.surface: A schoolchild throws out the old maths tools and topics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rulers' at the start looks like part of the maths list, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsars were the emperors of Russia, so they were monarchs who ruled.

clue.text: Abstract? See, I completely agree

parts.note: a precis is a summary or abstract
Ely is a cathedral city and the seat, or see, of a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone shown a summary says that's exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'see' is the diocese of a bishop; Ely is a small English cathedral city often used this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Said on its own as an exclamation, the word expresses total agreement, like 'exactly'.

clue.text: Division over Spanish article in Variety

indicators.note: the article goes inside the division

parts.note: a section is a part or division

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A department reviews a piece about Spain in the showbiz paper Variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is an assortment or range on offer, much like a variety.

clue.text: Nationalist not sure rioting seizes government

indicators.note: the rearranged letters seize, or hold, the extra one
rioting means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An uncertain political activist turns to unrest and takes over the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and was First Minister of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon was leader of the Scottish National Party, so she is a Scottish nationalist politician.

clue.text: Coup deposes king for progress

indicators.note: to depose is to remove from power, so the king is dropped

parts.note: a revolution is an overthrow, like a coup
R, for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A rebellion overthrows the monarch for the sake of advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is gradual development over time, a kind of progress.

clue.text: One travelling a long time during very ordinary year

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: the long time falls during, i.e. inside, the year

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A traveller spends ages on the road in a dull year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also hints at the Voyager space probes, travelling for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyager is a person making a long journey, so someone on their travels.

indicators.note: the division sign splits the string of letters and puts the divisor into the gap

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
I is the Roman numeral for 1
C again for 100
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A sum that looks like arithmetic homework.
explanation.walkthrough: The string CICK is split, or divided, by L, giving C L ICK.
explanation.definitionFit: When two people click they get on well instantly, an idiom for hitting it off.

clue.text: Prince Henry taken into vehicle by aliens, oddly vanishing

indicators.note: the letter is taken into the vehicle, so placed inside it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters vanish, leaving the even ones

parts.note: its even-placed letters, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Prince Harry is abducted by extraterrestrials in a car, which then mysteriously vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Henry' looks like one royal, but the prince is the definition and Henry only gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles was long Prince of Wales before becoming king, so a royal prince.

clue.text: Australian city turning inward

indicators.note: turning the letters about rearranges them

explanation.surface: A city in Australia is becoming introspective.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Gloomy character's blowing top over drugs and monstrosities

indicators.note: the name with its top gone goes over, or covers, the drugs
losing the top, i.e. the first letter

parts.note: Eeyore, the glum donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh, with the possessive S
Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: A melancholy figure loses his temper over narcotics and horrors.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first E from EEYORE'S leaves EYORES; Es (ecstasy) go in after its Y and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesores are ugly sights, such as hideous buildings, so monstrosities.

clue.text: Quiet game starting to get gesture of indifference

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the starting, or first, letter of get

parts.note: first letter G

explanation.surface: A low-key sport begins to produce an apathetic reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug is a raising of the shoulders that signals not caring.

clue.text: Wildcat gatecrashing a navy function?

indicators.note: the wild letters crash in, entering the navy's letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
read as 'wild cat': the letters of cat run wild, rearranged as CTA

explanation.surface: A wild animal barges into a naval party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildcat' is read as two words, wild signalling a rearrangement of CAT; 'function' looks like a party to crash, but it is the maths definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctan, the inverse tangent, is a trigonometric function in mathematics.

clue.text: Cliff's not very small trunks

indicators.note: not means lacking, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: torsos are bodies' trunks
so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: Someone named Cliff has swimming trunks that are not tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff's' reads like a man's name; it is the definition, with 's as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky outcrop on a hill, here loosely a crag or cliff.

clue.text: King George IV clings to throne, ultimately in era of trouble

indicators.note: the royal pieces sit inside the era

parts.note: an age is an era
GR, Georgius Rex

indicators.note: IV wraps itself around, clinging to, the letter
the last letter of throne

parts.note: last letter E

explanation.surface: A Regency monarch hangs on to power during a turbulent period.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to distress or wrong someone, so to trouble them.

clue.text: With indoor launderettes, outer layers get spins

indicators.note: taking only the outside letters of each word

parts.note: outer letters W and H
outer letters I and R
outer letters L and S

explanation.surface: Washing machines in laundromats turn clothes, with outer garments spun round.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirls are rapid turns or rotations, so spins.

clue.text: After losing billions, Russian drinks alcohol for starters

indicators.note: the shortened name drinks in, or contains, the alcohol
the letter is lost from the name

parts.note: Boris is a typical Russian man's name
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A Russian oligarch who has lost a fortune drinks spirits before the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' looks like a link meaning 'to begin with', but 'starters' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Origins are beginnings or starting points, so starters in that sense.

clue.text: Silliest place to find eggs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: most foolish or empty-headed
second meaning: read as three words, '...', where eggs are found

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer must be split into three words for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanest is the superlative of inane, meaning most senseless, and split up it reads 'in a nest'.
